correctness.rationale: All involutions have an underlying fixed-point/transposition decomposition with paired signs. Explicit fixed equations yield the complete exact positive spectrum and identical numerator for B_n and D_n. A uniform positive-parameter Poisson local-limit/saddle estimate for [z^n] exp(tz+z²) supplies the rare-event constant e^{3/8}; the t=0 parity term is exponentially negligible. Conditional exponential generating functions yield a Gaussian limit via the moment-generating-function continuity theorem. The standalone program exhaustively enumerates actual involutions and cube-vertex actions for n=1..6, and checks asymptotic constants numerically to n=1000; finite data do not prove the limit.

originality.rationale: The assessed new claim is the joint sharp stretched-exponential rare-event probability, including the type-D factor-two constant, and the conditional Gaussian fixed-affine-subspace dimension law. The exact fixed-point criterion of Chen (1992/1993) and the type-B/D involution recurrences (Gutierres et al., 2024) are explicitly credited, not claimed original. Arumugam et al. (2022) count fixed points over unrestricted wreath-product elements, whereas the present denominator is the involution subpopulation. published-finding corpus semantic searches for exact objects, aliases and probabilistic parameters did not identify either conditional asymptotic in the closest indexed scientific claims. This is best-knowledge originality, not a uniqueness certificate.

value.rationale: The question quantifies the naturally exceptional involutions of two classical reflection groups whose standard binary-cube action has any fixed vertices. The precise stretched-exponential rarity law, sharp type-D factor two, and Gaussian dimension of the conditional fixed affine spaces are substantial population-level invariants. They distinguish conditional derangement behavior from the well-known unrestricted wreath-product statistics; the already established exact fixed-point criterion is credited, not presented as an original achievement.
